summary: Live bench of myiotsan's deadband gate and telemetry read-back path against a real broker (tools/fleetbench/bench_iotsan_telemetry.py). The deadband gate itself held completely - first-sample admission, the >= boundary, a baseline that does not creep across a slow sub-deadband drift, heartbeat behavior, an edited deadband taking effect with no restart, and a suppressed sample still reaching the rule engine were all measured correct. The bench found real defects on the read-back half. TelemetryService.Latest folded a device's newest 500 rows to build "the current value of every key" for the device page, which crowds a quiet key off the page once a chatty key fills the shared tail (measured: 520 rows on one key hid the other six keys on a seven-key device); it now takes the profile's declared key list and does one indexed seek per key, falling back to the tail scan only for a device with no profile. Series() asked the database ascending, which discards the newest end of a window over the cap - a wide chart of a busy key drew the oldest slice and looked identical to a dead device; it now reads newest-first and reverses, and over the cap actually reads the rollup buckets (Rollups() had zero callers anywhere in the app before this) topped up with the unfolded raw tail, answering {items, span, truncated} instead of a bare list so a chart never silently swaps raw samples for hourly summaries without saying so. rollupOnce's cutoff was now-minus-width rather than a bucket boundary, which cuts mid-bucket and permanently undercounts the readings past the cut; the cutoff is now floored to the bucket boundary, and a new dropIncompleteTail guards a batch-filling pass from folding an unproven-whole trailing bucket. The rollup worker's interval was a hardcoded, unsettable hour, so it had never been observed running on any bench of this app; a new telemetry_store.rollupIntervalMs config field (default unchanged at 1h) makes it exercisable. DeadbandGate.Forget shipped with zero production callers despite the ingest path documenting the gate map as its one unbounded structure; device deletion now calls a new Ingest.ForgetDevice. ReadingWriter's written stat summed CreateMultiple's last-insert-id return value instead of counting rows, so it grew with table size rather than work done (2,666 readings reported as 3,555,111 written); it now counts rows handed to each batch. 50/50 checks passed with the fixes, 33/44 against the unfixed binary.
compatibility: Backward-compatible; no schema change. GET /api/devices/{id}/readings now answers {items, span, truncated} instead of a bare {items}; existing callers reading items are unaffected, and span/truncated are additive fields. GET /api/devices/{id}/latest's response shape is unchanged, only its internal query strategy. New config field telemetry_store.rollupIntervalMs defaults to 1 hour, matching the previously-hardcoded cadence exactly, so every existing install's rollup schedule is unchanged unless an operator sets it explicitly in config.json; it is deliberately not exposed in the runtime-editable Telemetry settings screen. Devices deleted before this change do not retroactively forget their deadband baseline (the gate map only clears going forward), which is a strict improvement with no regression risk. GET /api/devices/stats's written counter now reports materially smaller, correct numbers - any external alerting keyed on its prior (inflated, meaningless) magnitude should be recalibrated.
